note: He fits the stated profile on everything except the ability to pay right now. Professionally he is the archetype: an architect, ten years in a family design and architecture practice, now spinning up his own sauna manufacturing venture in Devon — 'successful, they own their own business' reads directly onto him. He is emphatically not deconditioned, which is where most of this batch fails; he plays competitive-standard squash, trained three to four times a week until a year ago, and follows Trevor's mobility work already. And the ask is refinement, not rescue: 'I wouldn't mind putting more shoulders, sort of chiseling it a bit more than what it was' and a spare tire that is 'not too big, but it's just not tight enough'. Health is the neglected corner of an otherwise ordered life — three months of renovation displaced it entirely. Income is the single miss and it is unambiguous: 'we're sort of breaking even almost, if you like. I'm just putting everything into the house' and 'I'm not sure I can fit nearly $1,000 a month on fitness'. What makes this a useful case for the rollup rather than just another edge is that the income miss is explicitly temporary — he named two months as the point at which it resolves. This is the strongest support yet for the existing corpus observation that income screening filters out deals a payment structure, or simply a later start date, could carry. Judged on the criteria as written he is an edge case; judged on the criteria as they will read in September, he is core.
